headline: Armadin, a cybersecurity start-up led by Kevin Mandia, formerly of the security firm Mandiant, has raised $255.5 million to build tools that block attacks automatically.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 1: the round was announced by 7 Oct 2026, before the 8 Oct window.
importance_line: What changed is a $2.5 billion bet that attackers using AI need defences that react just as fast, which matters first to company security teams that often wait days or weeks to apply permanent fixes, then to the security vendors Armadin plugs into, and the doubt is that the blocks are temporary stopgaps and the claims come from the company.
summary: BankInfoSecurity reports that Armadin's Series B round (a mid-stage investment round), led by Andreessen Horowitz and Accel, values the company at $2.5 billion and will fund tools that write temporary blocking rules, first through CrowdStrike's managed detection service, to stop an attack while customers prepare permanent fixes that co-founder Evan Pena says can take days or weeks. The round was already listed in a CyberWire briefing dated 7 Oct 2026, and Pena concedes the firewall blocks only help for a short time before attackers bypass them.
notes: Announcement predates 8 Oct (CyberWire briefing of 7 Oct); exact day not confirmed. Page blocked on the first fetch, read after decoding the Google News link.
